title: Cinema Schedule Gaps
statement:
Choose whether one more movie can fit into a theater day that already has screenings.

Contract
- Construct a schedule with `new Solution(movies, screenings)`. The theater opens at 10:00 and closes at 23:00.
- Each `Movie` has a title, duration in minutes, and revenue. Each `Screening` names a movie and start minute measured after midnight.
- Existing screenings may arrive unsorted; use their movie durations to find occupied intervals. Tests use non-overlapping existing screenings with known titles.
- `canSchedule(title)` returns true when the named movie can fit wholly inside any free gap between opening, existing screenings, and closing. Unknown titles return false.
- `calculateRevenue()` returns the sum of revenue from the existing screenings only.

Examples
- With `Short` lasting 60 minutes already at 10:00 and 12:00, a 90-minute `Feature` fits after 13:00 before closing.
- If a 700-minute `Epic` is requested between the fixed opening and closing time, it does not fit once a noon screening occupies part of the day.

examples.input: movies Short:60:100|Feature:90:250; screenings Short@10:00,Short@12:00; query Feature
movies Short:60:100|Epic:700:900; screenings Short@12:00; query Epic

hints: Convert times to minutes and sort existing screenings by start time before checking gaps.
Treat the opening-to-first and last-to-closing spans the same way as gaps between screenings.
Revenue is independent of the query movie; add the revenue of each existing screening once.
inputSyntax: Input: movie definitions, screenings, and query, for example: movies Short:60:100|Feature:90:250; screenings Short@10:00,Short@12:00; query Feature
sampleInput: movies Short:60:100|Feature:90:250; screenings Short@10:00,Short@12:00; query Feature
